claim: Demšar's paper recommending Wilcoxon signed-rank and Friedman-plus-post-hoc mean-ranks tests for ML benchmark comparisons was published in JMLR volume 7, issue 1, in 2006 -- a decade before, and a distinct paper from, Benavoli et al.'s 2016 JMLR 17 rebuttal.
stance_target: disambiguating Demšar 2006 from Benavoli 2016 in the citation ledger
quoted_support: "Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers over Multiple Data Sets. Janez Demšar; 7(1):1-30, 2006."

claim: Demšar recommends the Friedman test with post-hoc mean-ranks tests (and introduces CD diagrams) as the standard methodology for comparing multiple classifiers over multiple datasets -- the exact methodology that Benavoli et al. (2016) later show produces pool-dependent conclusions.
stance_target: establishing the methodological lineage between Demšar 2006 and Benavoli 2016
quoted_support: "we recommend a set of simple, yet safe and robust non-parametric tests ... the Friedman test with the corresponding post-hoc tests for comparison of more classifiers over multiple data sets. Results of the latter can also be neatly presented with the newly introduced CD (critical difference) diagrams."

claim: Demsar (2006) contains no numeric dataset-count threshold (e.g. 'more than ten datasets') anywhere in its 30 pages for when the Friedman omnibus test is recommended; its only 'ten data sets' references describe the paper's own random-subsampling power-simulation methodology, not a usage threshold.
stance_target: AAAI-27 draft's citation 'this omnibus is recommended for more than ten datasets \citep{demsar2006statistical}' (main.tex line 220)
scope_conditions: Full-text grep of the 30-page JMLR 2006 PDF (jmlr.org/papers/volume7/demsar06a/demsar06a.pdf), all instances of 'ten', 'recommend', and 'Friedman test'
quoted_support: The only instances of 'ten data sets' are: 'When comparing two classifiers, samples of ten data sets were randomly selected...' and 'selections of ten data sets, as described above' -- both describing the paper's OWN power-experiment sampling procedure (drawing 10 of 40 UCI datasets per trial), not a recommended minimum for using the omnibus test.

claim: Demsar's actual concluding recommendation is unconditional preference for non-parametric tests (Wilcoxon/Friedman) over parametric ones (t-test/ANOVA) for machine learning data, with no stated minimum dataset count gating when the Friedman/omnibus test becomes appropriate.
stance_target: correct characterization of what Demsar 2006 actually recommends, for citation-repair purposes
quoted_support: "Overall, the non-parametric tests, namely the Wilcoxon and Friedman test are suitable for our problems. They are appropriate since they assume some, but limited commensurability... Empirical results suggest that they are also stronger than the other tests studied."
